title: Leverage Your Own Economies of Scale
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This essay uses consumer product companies — Mars, PepsiCo, Taco Bell, Johnson & Johnson — to illustrate how a small set of core ingredients or components can be recombined into dozens of distinct products. It argues the same logic applies to leadership: enterprises that identify and nurture a small set of foundational competencies can achieve higher quality, greater consistency, and lower cost than competitors spread across a wider set of capabilities. The piece closes with a direct set of self-assessment questions asking readers to name their own organization's core ingredients and whether they're actively leveraged for scale.
points: Uses consumer brands (Mars, PepsiCo, Taco Bell, J&J) to illustrate how a small ingredient set can generate a wide, diverse product portfolio.
Argues concentrating on fewer core competencies allows an organization to source or produce them with higher quality and lower cost than a broadly spread competitor.
Frames economies of scale as a quality lever, not just a cost-cutting mechanism — mastery of fewer elements enables innovation on top of them.
Challenges readers directly to name their own organization's foundational competencies or 'core ingredients.'
Closes with the claim that leaders rarely improve quality by cutting costs, but genuine economies of scale let them cut costs by improving quality.
quotes: Mars knows what it means to leverage economies of scale. That’s a business school way of saying they use a core set of ingredients to create dozens of distinctive products to match consumer tastes.
Many of the best companies in the world focus on a core set of ingredients, elements, or ideas that they combine into a diverse set of products or services.

When a company relies on a small set of critical ingredients or elements, it can get very good at sourcing or producing them at the highest level of quality, with the greatest consistency, and at the lowest cost.

What competencies, core ingredients, critical skills, or essential elements does your enterprise depend upon? Can you point to a small set of elements that are more central to everything you do or stand for?
Leaders rarely improve quality by cutting costs, but economies of scale prove that they can cut costs by improving on quality.
